# Pa 30: An 845-Year-Old Cosmic Mystery

When medieval astronomers across China, Japan, and the Arab world spotted a brilliant "guest star" blazing in the sky for six months in 1181, they were witnessing a catastrophic cosmic collision—two dense stellar corpses called white dwarfs spiraling together and exploding in what's now called a Type Iax supernova. Today, the Gemini North Telescope in Hawai'i reveals the spectacular aftermath: the Pa 30 nebula, where an extremely hot central star blasts fierce winds that have sculpted glowing filaments studded with pearl-like knots the size of our entire solar system.
